CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR JUNE 6, 2022 AT 2:30 P.M. WILL TAKE PLACE
SOLELY BY VIDEOCONFERENCE/TELECONFERENCE.
City Council Meeting Policy:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-Meeting-Policy.pdf
In order to facilitate public participation at meetings held solely by
electronic means, the City will accept public comment in the following manner:
1. During the meeting, members of
the public may provide live public comment by submitting a speaker card prior to
the start of public comment on that item, at the following webpage:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
If a public comment speaker wishes to speak on more than one agenda item, please
indicate so on the online form (multiple item speakers will be handled according
to the process posted on the agenda and as specified in the City Council meeting
policy). Public comments are limited to 3 minutes each, and the Mayor and City
Council may limit this time if reasonable under the circumstances.
2. Speaker Card Help Line : If
a public comment speaker needs assistance in completing a speaker card, please
call the City Clerk’s Office at: (626) 744-4124. Help line will open
30 minutes prior to the posted
start time of the meeting.
After submitting a public speaker card, join the virtual meeting after the
published start time with a computer, other electronic device, or by telephone.
The same name or telephone number on the Speaker Card should be used for the
virtual meeting in order to locate and unmute the speaker.
Your phone call to the City Council
meeting will be recorded as part of the City Council meeting. By
staying on the line and making public comment during the City Council meeting,
you are agreeing to have your phone call recorded.
Computer or electronic devices, join the meeting at:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Telephone only dial-in: 1-669-900-6833, Meeting ID: 161 482 446
3. Members of the public may
submit correspondence of any length prior to the start of the meeting, at the
following email address:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
Correspondence will be forwarded to the City Council
prior to the start of the meeting, posted online, and made part of the
legislative record for the item.

LA REUNIÓN ESPECIAL DEL CONSEJO MUNICIPAL DEL 6 DE JUNIO DE 2022 A LAS 2:30 P.M.
TENDRÁ LUGAR ÚNICAMENTE POR VIDEOCONFERENCIA/TELECONFERENCIA.
City Council Meeting Policy:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-Meeting-Policy.pdf
Para facilitar la participación del público en reuniones realizadas únicamente
por medios electrónicos, la Ciudad aceptará comentarios del público de la
siguiente manera:
1. Durante la reunión, los miembros del
público pueden hacer comentarios públicos en vivo presentando una tarjeta de
oratoria antes del inicio del comentario sobre el artículo que se está tratando
en el siguiente sitio web:
www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment
Si un orador de comentario público desea hablar sobre más de un artículo del
orden del día, le solicitamos que lo indique en el formulario en línea (los
oradores sobre artículos múltiples se manejarán según el proceso publicado en la
agenda y lo especificado en la política sobre las reuniones el Consejo
Municipal). Los comentarios públicos se limitan a 3 minutos cada uno y el
Alcalde y el Consejo Municipal pueden limitar este tiempo si lo consideran
razonable para las circunstancias.
2. Línea
de ayuda de la tarjeta de oratoria pública :
Si un orador de comentario público
necesita asistencia para completar su tarjeta, puede llamar
a la Oficina del
Secretario de la Ciudad al
(626) 744-4124. La línea de ayuda abrirá 30
minutos antes del inicio de la reunión.
Después de presentar una tarjeta de oratoria pública, únase a la reunión virtual
a la hora de inicio publicada con una computadora, otro dispositivo electrónico
o por
teléfono. Debe usar el
mismo nombre o número de teléfono de la tarjeta de oratoria para la reunión
virtual de modo que se pueda ubicar y habilitar el audio para el
orador.
Su llamada telefónica a la reunión del Concejo
Municipal se grabará como parte de la
reunión del Concejo Municipal. Al permanecer en la línea y hacer
comentarios públicos durante la
reunión del Concejo Municipal, está aceptando que se grabe su llamada
telefónica.
Computadoras y dispositivos electrónicos pueden sumarse a la reunión en:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446
Número para ingresar a la reunión por teléfono: 1-669-900-6833, ID de la
reunión: 161 482 446
3. Los miembros del público
pueden enviar correspondencia de cualquier longitud antes del inicio de
la reunión a la siguiente dirección de correo electrónico:
correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
La
correspondencia se enviará al Consejo Municipal antes del inicio de la reunión,
se publicará en línea, y se incorporará al registro legislativo sobre el
artículo.

CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  June 6, 2022 - 2:30 P.M.

I  City Hall Council Chamber

  The special meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

  OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the special meeting to order at 2:34 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Steve Haderlein, President of the
  Rose Bowl Operating Company President.

  ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy (Arrived at 2:37 p.m.)
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  Interim City Manager Cynthia Kurtz
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  CONSENT CALENDAR  RECOMMENDED FISCAL YEAR 2023 ROSE BOWL OPERATING
  COMPANY OPERATING BUDGET

I  Recommendation of the Rose Bowl Operating Company
  (RBOC}: It is recommended that the City Council authorize the
  inclusion of the proposed Fiscal Year 2023 Rose Bowl Operating
  Company Operating Budget in the City Manager's Recommended
  Operating Budget for Fiscal Year 2023.

  Steve Haderlein, RBOC President, provided introductory comments.
  Darryl Dun, Chief Executive Officer & General Manager, introduced
  Jens Weiden, Chief Revenue Officer, and Mo Salama, Controller,
  who presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item; and
  responded to questions.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that seven letters advocating for a
  complete analysis of the Rose Bowl Stadium revenue model,
  including its relationship to the convention center and broader civic
  marketing revenue streams, as well as direct income brought in by
  the stadium; opposing the use of City General Funds or reserve funds
  to pay Rose Bowl debt; and providing comments on the matter; and
  twenty-three letters in support of the Rose Bowl Stadium's economic,
  cultural, and community importance to Pasadena, including that the
  Rose Bowl Stadium is an important City asset and a vital source of
  opportunities for small businesses, with all correspondence received

I  by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City Council, posted on-
  line, and made part of the public record.

  Council Minutes  1  06/06/2022
   Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Madison,
  seconded by Councilmember Masuda, to approve the staff
  recommendation to include the RBOC's Fiscal Year (FY) 2023

I  Operating Budget as part of the City Manager's FY 2023
  Recommended Operating Budget:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Kennedy, Madison, Masuda,
  Rivas, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor Gordo
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: None

  CONSIDERATION OF ROSE BOWL OPERATING COMPANY
  {RBOC) FIVE-YEAR STRATEGIC INITIATIVES
  Recommendation of the Rose Bowl Operating Company
  (RBOC): It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Authorize the General Manager, on behalf of the City Council, to:
  a. Diligently pursue the following revenue generating
  opportunities in a pre-development phase:
  i.  Family Golf Center;
  ii. Campus Marque/Sponsorship Program;
  iii. Sponsorship 210 freeway signage;
  iv. Alignment of interests in contracts with UCLA and
  Tournament of
  Roses;

I  v. South End Zone seating project;
  vi. Analysis of a potential citywide parking tax on paid
  parking spaces;
  vii. A potential increase of Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT);
  viii. Third-party funding opportunities related to future capital
  improvements;
  b. Explore additional opportunities in the Rose Bowl area that
  would broaden the monetization opportunities while being
  cognizant of acceptable use within the Arroyo Seco; and
  (2) Direct the Interim City Manager to work together with the Rose
  Bowl Operating Company (RBOC) General Manager, and report to
  the RBOC and City Council (or designated City Council Committee)
  quarterly with updates on progress.

  Mayor Gordo and General Manager Darryl Dunn, provided
  introductory comments, Dan Barrett, President, CAA ICON Strategic
  Advisory, Jens Weiden, Chief Revenue Officer, and Michael Ross,
  CEO, Pasadena Center Operating Company (PCOC), presented a
  PowerPoint presentation on the item; and all responded to questions.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that four letters advocating for the Rose

I  Bowl Operating Company to sell the naming rights of the Rose Bowl
  Stadium to raise money; insisting that the City Council and RBOC
  have a thorough public discussion on various suggested options for
  increasing the RBOC revenues; urging that the City and RBOC to

  Council Minutes  2  06/06/2022
   consider options for additional tax revenue streams to stabilize and
  fund the stadium, and noting that solutions must take into account the
  importance of preserving the Arroyo Seco and surrounding open

I  space, including the Central Arroyo, as protected resources of the
  City; as well expressing concerns with RBOC hiring a new General
  Manager without conducting a national search; with one letter
  received in opposition to RBOC significantly altering the Rose Bowl
  Stadium, which is a Historic Landmark; and twelve letters advocating
  for additional City funding for the Arroyo Link in the Measure R project
  list, which were received by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the
  City Council, posted on-line, and made part of the public record.

  The following individuals provided comments on the agenda item:

  Sonja Berndt, Pasadena resident
  Nina Chomsky, Linda Vista-Annandale Association

  Vice Mayor Wilson spoke in support of pursuing a holistic approach
  in energizing the Arroyo Seco and Rose Bowl stadium more
  aggressively by allocating additional resources and funding towards
  conceptual designs and plans, as well as the need for collaboration
  between the RBOC and One Arroyo Foundation in pursuing a
  restructuring and reimagining of the Rose Bowl and the Arroyo Seco
  area as a world class destination for wellness, recreation and
  entertainment. Vice Mayor Wilson expressed concerns with a

I  piecemeal approach that only addresses the capital needs
  assessment related to improvements and repairs of the stadium.

  Councilmember Williams thanked staff for presentation and the
  additional fiscal detail regarding the Rose Bowl subsidy payments
  made from the General Fund. She noted her concerns with the
  suggested revenue enhancements as presented in the strategic plan,
  stating she is more in support of long-term solutions, such as a new
  tenant relationship, infusion of tax revenue, and/or a restructuring of
  the bond debt as a way to provide fiscal stability to the Rose Bowl.
  Councilmember Williams advocated for accountability and
  transparency in terms of stadium revenue and expenditure reporting
  given that the money invested in the Rose Bowl is public funds. She
  also spoke on the need for a community benefits plan and
  subsequent reporting from the Rose Bowl, to illustrate the number of
  local jobs generated, the number of high school graduations hosted,
  and what other stadium programs occurred that Pasadena residents
  are served by and benefit from as a City resource. She recommended
  that staff return with an evaluation of various structures that will allow
  the City to put taxpayer money into the stadium in a way that is
  transparent and provides stability, as opposed to pursuing riskier

I  options (i.e. mini golf), and suggested that the Rose Bowl Ad Hoc
  Committee review the proposed options and provide a
  recommendation to the City Council prior to the expiration of the
  current operating agreement between the City and RBOC.

  Council Minutes  3  06/06/2022
   Councilmember Hampton thanked staff for the presentation, stating
  that the economic impact report was much needed; suggested
  consideration be given to opening the Ad Hoc Committee meeting

I  and discussion to the public, and expressed support for further
  discussion on the proposed revenue generating opportunities
  presented in the report, stating each matter should be vetted one by
  one to determine how and/or if to move forward with the each item as
  part of the overall strategic plan initiative.

  Councilmember Masuda thanked the members of the RBOC and
  PCOC for the presentation; stated that structural improvements to the
  stadium should be a priority, and expressed support to further discuss
  the potential to increase the number of music events, development
  around the stadium, potential increases to Transit Occupancy Tax
  (TOT) and/or a city-wide parking tax to provide additional sources of
  revenue to support the stadium.

  Councilmember Kennedy requested information on the creation of
  the City's operating companies, including why they were formed,
  noting that the Legacy Foundation and its relationship to the RBOC
  have not been revisited in recent public discussions, specifically in
  light of the City's General Fund payments made in support of the
  Rose Bowl bond debt and compensation issues related to the highest
  paid employees. He asked staff to provide a clear understanding
  regarding the feasibility of refinancing the Rose Bowl bonds, as well

I  as the viability of the proposed development opportunities around the
  Rose Bowl (as suggested in the strategic plan), requesting the City
  Attorney provide a determination on the conflicting viewpoints related
  to development of open space (what can and cannot be done), prior
  to pursuing such revenue opportunities as potential models to pay
  debt and/or reinvest in the iconic Rose Bowl. Councilmember
  Kennedy thanked staff and the consultants for the presentation,
  expressed his appreciation and gratitude to Daryl Dunn for his long-
  serving leadership and dedication to the success of the Rose Bowl
  and benefits provided to the community.

  Councilmember Madison spoke on the Rose Bowl New Year's Day
  legacy, the consensus of the City Council to preserve the iconic Rose
  Bowl Stadium by supporting the renovation project, commented on
  the unique nature of the Rose Bowl being nestled between beautiful
  neighborhoods and being municipally owned, and spoke on
  increased competition from local facilities such as SoFi Stadium in
  Inglewood, stating given the special needs of the Rose Bowl, he feels
  the RBOC structure has worked well, and commended the RBOC for
  their tremendous work and transparency. Councilmember Madison
  touched upon the Vice Mayor's comments related to pursing a

I  strategic review, stating he would support some sort of contribution
  or enhancement to the RBOC's budget as a way to move forward
  with the holistic strategic initiative/review of the Rose Bowl and Arroyo
  Seco.

  Council Minutes  4  06/06/2022
   Councilmember Rivas spoke in support of the sentiment that the City
  Council needs to keep an open mind and keep everything on the
  table, stating it is not clear at this point, that the structure of the RBOC

I  is the issue but is open to further discussion on the matter.

  Mayor Gordo spoke on the history of the Rose Bowl, stating that the
  initial intent of the stadium as an economic development asset to
  bring tourism to Pasadena continues today. The Mayor stated the
  City has the responsibility to protect the stadium as an economic
  engine, which supports local businesses, and in turn the City's
  General Fund, by generating incremental tax dollars throughout the
  year, and on January 1st the Rose Bowl captures the world's
  attention, noting the City has a responsibility to act deliberately and
  thoughtfully. He also acknowledged the City must maintain a delicate
  balance given that the Rose Bowl is located in the middle of parkland
  and neighborhoods. The Mayor stated he would work with the City
  Manager and the RBOC General Manager to determine the next
  steps, and suggested hosting a City Council workshop, asking the
  Rose Bowl Ad Hoc Committee to help staff craft the agenda for the
  workshop.

  Vice Mayor Wilson expressed his support for a workshop, stating
  topics of discussion should include whether there is consensus to
  generate revenue for the Rose Bowl by tapping into City tax streams
  (potential increases to Transit Occupancy Tax (TOT) and/or a city-

I  wide parking tax), and/or by increasing revenue through the
  introduction of enhancing and creating more activities in and around
  the Rose Bowl.

  Mayor Gordo and Vice Mayor Wilson expressed thanks to
  Councilmember William's for requesting a report on the economic
  impact of the Rose Bowl and requested that staff post the report on
  the City's website.

  By consensus of the City Council, and on order of the Mayor, the
  information was received and filed.

  ADJOURNMENT  On pi= er of the Mayor, the special meeting of the City Council
  adjour ed at 4:36 p.

  ~~W\-
  Victor M. Gordo, M  o
  City of Pasadena
